record_order_vs_c.rule: each scanner writes a reply's status record and then its banners in the order the replies arrive on its own wire (judged per step); the two runs of a document do not get the same reply order from the stand (one responder thread per UDP socket), so rmasscan's status and banner records must equal C's field for field but the time in any order: the set of banners per (address, port, application) is C's; a TCP connection's banners come when it is destroyed, in an order its scenario's timing decides, so the same rule holds for them

notes.reply_order_window: 50 us: two replies captured on the peer link at most this far apart (rounded to the microsecond; exactly 50 us is inside) may reach the scanner in the other order (two CPUs send them); reply_order_swaps gives, per step, the pairs of records written in the other order within it (pairs) and the largest gap among them in microseconds (largest_gap_us, null without such a pair)

record_order_vs_c.rule: each scanner writes a reply's status record and then its banners in the order the replies arrive on its own wire (judged per step); the two runs of a document do not get the same reply order from the stand (one responder thread per UDP socket), so rmasscan's status and banner records must equal C's field for field but the time in any order: the set of banners per (address, port, application) is C's; a TCP connection's banners come when it is destroyed, in an order its scenario's timing decides, so the same rule holds for them

notes.reply_order_window: 50 us: two replies captured on the peer link at most this far apart (rounded to the microsecond; exactly 50 us is inside) may reach the scanner in the other order (two CPUs send them); reply_order_swaps gives, per step, the pairs of records written in the other order within it (pairs) and the largest gap among them in microseconds (largest_gap_us, null without such a pair)

scanner_frame_classes.answers_for_source: TCP resolve cases: the scanner's ARP reply or Neighbor Advertisement for its own source address, one per request of the peer (C src/main.c:878-887, src/stack-ndpv6.c:95-182)
scanner_frame_classes.arp_reply_for_scanner: the scanner's own ARP reply to the peer's who-has for 198.18.0.1, both scanners alike: C answers from its receive loop (src/main.c:878-887, stack_arp_incoming_request src/stack-arpv4.c:282-363), rmasscan's responder the same, 60 bytes to the requester; judged against the requests (none while the peer keeps its permanent neighbour entry)
scanner_frame_classes.heartbeats: TCP cases: the peer's heartbeat, a lab marker frame every 200 ms that keeps C's receive loop turning (counted, from the peer)
scanner_frame_classes.kernel_arp_reply_for_scanner: the scanner namespace kernel's 42-byte ARP reply to the same who-has (198.18.0.1 is its address)
scanner_frame_classes.next_hop_who_has: the scanner's next-hop resolution: an ARP who-has 198.18.0.2 from 198.18.0.1, 60 bytes zero-padded (the resolver form of C stack-arpv4.c and rmasscan), in a scan that is no ARP scan
scanner_frame_classes.port_unreachable_to_udp_reply: an ICMP 3/3 from 198.18.0.1 quoting a UDP reply of the stand: the scanner namespace kernel, no socket on the source port
scanner_frame_classes.protocol_unreachable_to_sctp_reply: an ICMP 3/2 from 198.18.0.1 quoting an SCTP INIT-ACK or ABORT of the stand: the scanner namespace kernel, no SCTP
scanner_frame_classes.rst_to_syn_ack: the scanner namespace kernel's reset of a SYN-ACK no socket owns (198.18.0.1 is its address): a TCP RST (no other flag) from 198.18.0.1 whose sequence number is the acknowledgment of a SYN-ACK of the stand, in any form but the SYN template's (that one is stateless_rst)
scanner_frame_classes.scrubbed_tcb_segments: TCP cases, C only: a segment of a TCB C destroyed earlier in the same frame, from and to 255.255.255.255:65535 (E1.5, no-frame-from-destroyed-tcb)
scanner_frame_classes.stack_segments: TCP cases: the scanner's segments of a connection the stand opened (its user-mode stack with --banners, the stateless RST without), compared with C's per connection
scanner_frame_classes.stateless_rst: the scanner's own stateless RST (R8), both scanners alike: C resets each distinct TCP reply (SYN-ACK or RST) that passed its cookie check and dedup (src/main.c:1048-1101: TCP_IS_SYNACK || TCP_IS_RST, dedup_is_duplicate, then tcp_send_RST when neither --banners nor --noreset), rmasscan the same (rmasscan_core::tcp_frame::stateless_rst); the frame is the probe's SYN template with seq the reply's acknowledgment, ack 0, flags 0x04, window 1200 (autodetect_verify::is_stateless_rst)
